Entrepreneurial

/on-truh-pruh-NUR-ee-uhl/ - the stress falls on NUR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Entrepreneurial means having the drive and imagination to start and run new businesses.

Even as a hospital custodian, Vanna had an entrepreneurial eye: she noticed the night-shift vending machines always sat empty and won the contract to restock them herself.

Worked Example

When streaming emptied her video store, the owner refused to wait for the customers to come back. She opened a phone-repair counter, then a board-game cafe in the freed-up aisles, then a rental service for party equipment. Each venture was small; together they showed an entrepreneurial instinct for spotting the next gap before the last business closed.

Entrepreneurial is more specific than 'driven' or 'hardworking': it names the particular drive to spot an opportunity and build a new venture around it, risks and all.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — self-starting → enterprising → entrepreneurial

self-starting vs. entrepreneurial

self-starting vs. entrepreneurial: A self-starting employee begins work without being told; entrepreneurial reaches further - starting not just tasks but whole ventures.

enterprising vs. entrepreneurial

enterprising vs. entrepreneurial: An enterprising scout finds clever ways to sell the most cookies; entrepreneurial goes a step beyond, naming the drive to build and run new businesses outright.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of entrepreneurial.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — entre-

Prefix — entre-: between, in (French, from Latin inter)

Root — pren-

Root — pren-: to take

Suffix — -eur

Suffix — -eur: one who

Suffix — -ial

Suffix — -ial: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Entre- (between, in) + pren- (to take) + -eur (one who) + -ial (relating to) = relating to one who takes things in hand. French entreprendre means 'to undertake,' so an entrepreneur is literally 'one who takes it upon herself' - and the adjective describes that taking-in-hand spirit applied to new ventures.

Word Choice

neutral / business

Entrepreneurial praises initiative pointed at building something new, usually a business. Enterprising is the broader compliment for resourcefulness anywhere; proactive, its unit-mate, is initiative aimed at preventing problems rather than launching ventures. Reach for entrepreneurial when the story involves spotting a market gap and taking the risk to fill it.
